title: Extension by zero and closed direct image preserve $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$
statement:
Let $X$ be a standing (Noetherian) scheme, $j\colon U\hookrightarrow X$ an open
immersion and $i\colon Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion.

1. $j_!\colon\D(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)\to\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ and
   $i_*\colon\D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)\to\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ map
   $\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, respectively $\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E)$
   into $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Hence so does $a_!=i_*u_!$ for every locally
   closed immersion $a=i\circ u\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ ($u$ open, $i$ closed).
2. Every $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ lies in the smallest full subcategory of
   $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ that is closed under isomorphisms and
   extensions (if two vertices of a distinguished triangle lie in it, so does
   the third) and contains the objects $a_!M$, where
   $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion of a stratum of a finite
   stratification and $M\in\Dbc(S,\mathcal O_E)$ is pro-étale locally on $S$ of the
   form $P\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_{E,S}$ for a bounded complex $P$ of finite
   free $\mathcal O_E$-modules.

proof.text: For an open immersion, apply the existing constructible extension-by-zero theorem to every homology sheaf. The exact functor homology comparison transports this to the homology of the derived image, and the bounded-map theorem preserves the bounds. For a closed immersion, take its open complement, obtain exactness from condensed recollement, and use the constructible closed-image theorem. Compare the ordinary derived map with the right derived functor. Applying the open and closed assertions successively proves the locally closed assertion.

Identify the coefficient ring used by the integral local finite-free resolution with the statement coefficient ring. Equip E with its spectral norm, shrink its carrier to universe zero using finite dimensionality over Q_l, and give the shrink the induced norm. The extending valuation identifies the two integer subrings with the closed unit ball. The resulting isometric ring equivalence induces an isomorphism of continuous-function ring sheaves, and hence of their commutative condensed ring objects. Restriction of scalars across the pulled-back ring isomorphism transports finite presentations, local freeness and short exact sequences.

proof.text: A locally finite free sheaf M has an allowed scalar complex model in degree zero. On a free pro-etale cover choose its rank n and take the single complex on the rank-n free module at the coefficient point. Pullback preserves the regular module and finite biproducts. The exact single-functor comparisons identify the pullback of M[0] with the pulled-back scalar complex. Its terms outside zero are zero and are free of rank zero; its support bounds are both zero. Thus the generator hypothesis applies to the extension of M[0] along any open immersion followed by a closed immersion. Present that locally closed immersion as the middle stratum of the explicit three-stratum stratification: the open complement of the closed image, the given open of the closed scheme, and its closed complement.

source.place: Clause (2): integral-heart resolution and finite open/closed localization

proof.text: For every locally finitely presented sheaf on such an open, use the integral local finite-free resolution, transported across the coefficient isomorphism, to obtain a short exact sequence with both resolving sheaves locally finite free. The degree-zero short exact triangle, mapped by exact open extension and closed pushforward, shows by the third two-out-of-three condition that its extension belongs to P. Use the single-functor comparison and the right-derived/ordinary-derived comparison to identify this object with the locally closed single-sheaf piece.

source.place: Clause (2): integral-heart resolution and finite open/closed localization

proof.text: Apply the existing coefficient-generic finite open/closed extension tower to each constructible sheaf. Every piece belongs to P by the previous step. Induct on the finite extension-product length using the second two-out-of-three condition, obtaining P for every constructible sheaf in degree zero. This includes zero, so P contains zero. Contractible distinguished triangles give closure under shifts by 1 and -1; integer induction gives every shift. The existing bounded derived-category devissage theorem, whose proof uses the finite canonical truncation triangles, now applies to the constructible homology sheaves of K and proves P K. This retains finite open/closed localization along strata and the integral-heart finite-free resolution route; it avoids constructing simultaneous whole-complex scalar models on a refined stratification.
